h1: The 7 Best Halloween Projectors for Your House of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven Halloween projector lights for house fronts, scored on waterproofing, timers, projection angle, scenes and installation.
summary: The dual-head IP65 projector with a timer is our top pick for a full house front, because two heads cover more wall and it is rated for rain. The 3-in-1 with a 160-degree head is the most flexible, HoneyFair's 12-in-1 offers the most scenes, and the PEIDUO and IP44 units are the cheap entry points.
intro: A Halloween projector is the one decoration where distance matters more than brightness. Throw a ghost scene across a wide lawn and it dims into a smudge, while the same projector close to a garage door shows up crisp. Where you plant the stake, and how large a wall it must cover, decides whether the effect looks sharp or washed out.

We ranked seven Halloween projector lights for house fronts by comparing what each listing states: waterproof rating, timer, projection angle, scene count and installation method. Very few give a lumen or range figure, so we say so, and we favor the units that let you aim and weatherproof the lamp. All are low-cost lights, priced from under $25 to $50.

products.name: Halloween Projector Lights Outdoor Dynamic Halloween Decorations with Timer
products.verdict: A dual-head projector with a timer and an IP65 waterproof rating.
products.description:
This outdoor projector uses a dual projector head design with a timer function, energy saving operation and an IP65 waterproof rating.

It leads because two heads can cover two surfaces, such as a garage door and a porch wall, or one wide facade, with a single stake and power run. IP65 is also the strongest waterproof rating stated in this group, which matters when October storms soak a lawn. The timer saves you from switching it on each night.

Buy it for a house front with more than one wall to light. The listing gives no throw distance or brightness figure, so test placement on a dark evening before you commit to a spot.
products.idealFor: Houses with two walls or a wide facade to cover.
products.skipIf: You need a stated range for a deep front yard.

products.name: 3 in 1 Halloween Projector Lights
products.verdict: Three interchangeable themes and a head that tilts up to 160 degrees.
products.description:
This projector offers dynamic Halloween scenes with three interchangeable themes, upgraded high-brightness LED chips and a 160-degree adjustable projector head with flexible placement.

It ranks second because a head that tilts up to 160 degrees lets you aim at a roofline, a window or a door from awkward angles, which is more useful than a fixed-angle stake. The brighter LED chips are a claim without a lumen number, so judge it by placement. It lacks the dual heads of the leader and gives no waterproof rating.

Buy it for a porch or window where you need to aim the light. Check weather protection on the live page before using it in rain.
products.idealFor: Porches and windows needing an angled projection.
products.skipIf: You need a rated outdoor weather seal.

products.name: HoneyFair 12 in 1 Halloween Ghost Projector Light Waterproof Outdoor Decor
products.verdict: Twelve switchable 3D scenes, four LED colors and a timer, indoors or out.
products.description:
HoneyFair's 12-in-1 offers switchable 3D Halloween scenes, a 4-color LED light change and a timer, rated as waterproof and ready for indoor and outdoor use.

It ranks third because twelve scenes let you change the look nightly, which keeps repeat visitors from seeing the same ghost twice. The 4-color LED change adds mood, but the listing states no IP rating beyond waterproof, so it sits below the IP65 dual-head unit for storm confidence.

Buy it for a house that gets many return visitors, or for a display you want to switch from spooky to gothic. Confirm the waterproof grade before leaving it out all season.
products.idealFor: Houses with repeat visitors who like a changing show.
products.skipIf: You need a stated storm-proof rating.

products.name: Halloween Projector Lights Outdoor
products.verdict: Three installation methods and a head that rotates 270 degrees, under $25.
products.description:
This waterproof outdoor projector lists a dynamic scene, three installation methods and a head that rotates 270 degrees for flexible angle adjustment.

It ranks fourth because three installation methods mean you can stake it, mount it or place it on a surface, depending on whether you have a lawn or a porch rail. That, plus the 270-degree rotation, suits oddly shaped fronts. It does not state a timer or an IP rating, so it trails the leader on automation and weather proof.

Buy it for an awkward house front where a fixed stake will not work. Under $25, it is also the cheapest of the aimable units.
products.idealFor: Awkward house fronts where a stake will not work.

products.name: HoneyFair Halloween Decoration Outdoor
products.verdict: Gothic horror shadows with sharp 3D detail and an adjustable setup.
products.description:
HoneyFair's outdoor projector creates a spooky scene with 3D gothic horror shadows and sharp projection details, with an adjustable projection setup.

It ranks fifth because its strength is image character, not features: no timer, no IP rating and no scene count appear in the listing. The sharp projection claim is the reason to choose it over the plain ghost units, as a crisper image holds up better on brick and siding.

Buy it for a house that wants a moody gothic look rather than cartoon ghosts, especially on pale brick or a light garage door where fine shadow detail stays visible. Without weatherproofing detail, shelter it under an eave, and confirm the stake or stand type on the live page before ordering.
products.idealFor: Homes that want a moody, gothic display.
products.skipIf: You need a timer or rated weather protection.

products.name: Halloween Lights Projector
products.verdict: A 3-in-1 projector with an IP44 rating and a timer for under $25.
products.description:
This projector lists three-in-one decorations, an IP44 waterproof rating and a timer, under $25.

It ranks sixth because IP44 protects against splashing water but not sustained jets, so it sits below the IP65 dual-head model for storms. The timer and three-in-one function are good value at this price, and it uses a single head, so coverage is narrower than the leader.

Buy it for a covered porch or entry where rain will not hit directly and the cable can run to an indoor outlet. Put it under an overhang, not on an open lawn, and bring it in if a storm is forecast, since splash-level protection ends where sustained rain begins.
products.idealFor: Covered porches and entries on a budget.
products.skipIf: The projector will sit on an open, rainy lawn.

products.name: PEIDUO Halloween Projector Lights
products.verdict: A simple ghost projector for indoors and out, quick to install.
products.description:
PEIDUO sells Halloween ghost projector lights for indoor and outdoor decorations, with quick and easy installation, under $25.

It ranks last because the listing offers no waterproof grade, timer or head adjustment, so it is the most basic option. Its virtue is simplicity: plug in, aim and go, with fewer parts to fail than the multi-scene units.

Buy it for a quick, low-cost ghost effect on a window or door, or as a backup unit in case a pricier projector fails mid-season. Do not leave it in heavy rain without confirming the weather protection, and expect to move it closer to the wall for a sharp picture.
products.idealFor: A quick ghost effect on a window or door.
products.skipIf: You want scene variety or a timer.

methodology.description: IP ratings and waterproof claims decide whether a projector survives an October storm, so stated grades earned weight.

methodology.description: Scene counts and themes keep a display fresh over the season, so we credited switchable designs.

whatMatters.detail: IP ratings show how well a case resists dust and water. IP44 handles splashes, while IP65 resists water jets, so it copes with heavy rain. The dual-head model lists IP65, and the Halloween Lights Projector lists IP44. Check the rating in the title or bullets, and shelter anything that only says waterproof.

The angle of the head sets which surface you can light. A head that tilts 160 degrees or rotates 270 degrees lets you aim up at a roof or sideways at a door without moving the stake. Check the stated range of motion, and match it to the layout of your front yard.

Scenes are the images or animations the lens cycles through. The 12-in-1 offers twelve, the 3-in-1 offers three, and many units give none. More scenes keep the display fresh for repeat visitors. Check whether scenes are switchable, since some units only loop a fixed pattern, and look for a theme that suits your house, because a ghost on a bright garage door reads better than a detailed bat scene on dark siding.

A timer turns the projector on and off on a schedule, so you do not have to remember each night. It also saves power and stops the lamp running all day. Look for a timer in the bullets, and check whether it is fixed hours or adjustable. Fixed settings suit trick-or-treat evenings, but a unit that stays lit all night annoys neighbors and shortens the life of the LED.

Brightness and distance decide how sharp the image appears on a wall. None of these listings states a lumen figure or range. Place the projector closer to the surface than you think you need, and test on a dark night before you stake it permanently. Also keep street lights and porch bulbs out of the image path, because ambient light flattens the picture faster than distance does.

faq.q: Can I leave a Halloween projector out in the rain?
faq.a: Only if it carries a suitable rating. The dual-head unit lists IP65, which resists heavy rain. The IP44 model handles splashes, so shelter it under a porch. For units with no stated grade, treat them as covered-use only.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with these projectors?
faq.a: Placing them too far from the surface. Small LED projectors dim quickly with distance, so the image washes out. Move the HoneyFair or PEIDUO closer to the wall until the picture is sharp, and test at night.

faq.q: Is the dual-head unit worth it over a single-head one?
faq.a: For a wide house front, yes. Two heads cover more wall and the IP65 rating copes with storms. For a single door or window, the IP44 Halloween Lights Projector at under $25 is enough.

faq.q: How do I set up a Halloween projector?
faq.a: Stake it or mount it level, aim it at a flat, light-colored wall and plug it in after dark to check focus. On the 3-in-1 or the 270-degree unit, adjust the head until the image fills the surface.

faq.q: How do I store them after Halloween?
faq.a: Dry the lens, wrap the cord loosely and store the unit in a dry box. Remove any batteries or adapters if the unit has them, and wipe the stake. Keep the lens covered to avoid scratches.

faq.q: Will a projector work on dark siding?
faq.a: Poorly. Projections need a light, flat surface to show up. Dark brick or siding absorbs the image. Use a garage door, a white sheet or a light wall, and aim the HoneyFair gothic scenes at pale surfaces.

finalTake: The dual-head IP65 Halloween projector is the one to buy for a house front: two heads, a timer and the strongest rain rating in the group. The 3-in-1 with a 160-degree head is the best for awkward angles, and the HoneyFair 12-in-1 gives you the most scenes. The IP44 Halloween Lights Projector and the PEIDUO cover covered porches and quick setups for under $25.
